references.text: Paul confirms the same tradition that Christ was raised and appeared to Cephas (Simon Peter), which corresponds directly with the Lord having "appeared to Simon" ([ref:1 Kor 15:4-5|1 Corinthians 15:4-5]).

The angels at the tomb had already proclaimed that Jesus had risen – "He is not here; he has risen" – and now the disciples confirm this with the words "The Lord has indeed risen" ([ref:Luk 24:6|Luke 24:6]).
In the Gospel of Mark, the young man at the tomb proclaims: "He has risen," the same message that the disciples now repeat with joy ([ref:Mark 16:6|Mark 16:6]).

The angel specifically says that the disciples should tell this to Peter – Simon is thus named here as well, which aligns with the fact that the risen one appeared to Simon ([ref:Mark 16:7|Mark 16:7]).

John notes that this was the third time Jesus appeared to his disciples after the resurrection, underscoring the pattern of repeated appearances, including the one to Simon ([ref:Joh 21:14|John 21:14]).
Peter himself testifies on Pentecost: "This Jesus God has raised up, and we are all witnesses." He confirms the resurrection he was among the first to experience ([ref:Apg 2:32|Acts 2:32]).

Peter preaches to Cornelius that God raised Jesus on the third day and allowed him to appear – not to all the people, but to witnesses whom God had chosen beforehand ([ref:Apg 10:40-41|Acts 10:40-41]).

Jesus himself confirms the resurrection with the words: "Thus it is written: The Messiah must suffer and rise from the dead on the third day." The phrase "has indeed risen" in verse 34 points forward to this confirmation ([ref:Luk 24:46|Luke 24:46]).

Luke writes in Acts that after his suffering Jesus "appeared to them over a period of forty days, showing himself by many convincing proofs," which supports the reality of the resurrection ([ref:Apg 1:3|Acts 1:3]).

Paul writes that Christ died and came back to life to be Lord of both the living and the dead – the title "the Lord" (ὁ κύριος) in Luke 24:34 underscores precisely this lordship of the risen one ([ref:Rom 14:9|Romans 14:9]).
